Heard, learned counsel for the parties.

Petitioner above-named who is in custody since 27.02.2024 has moved this Court for grant of regular bail in connection with Kotwali [Ranchi] P.S. Case No.161 of 2020 [G.R. No.374 of 2022]
registered under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468 & 120B of the Indian Penal Code.
As per the prosecution case, the informant entered into a development agreement with the land owner Shankar Dayal Singh (since dead) on 27.06.2008 and paid Rs.16,10,000/- to him.

Shankar Dayal Singh died in the year 2011 and thereafter his wife entered into supplementary agreement on 02.06.2012 with the informant and she was paid Rs.5,00,000/-in which this petitioner signed as a witness.

Informant repeatedly requested the appellant to hand over the premise after getting it vacated from the tenant, so that he could proceed with the work, but the property was not handed over to the Petitioner.
It is said that thereafter the wife and son of the deceased Shankar Dayal Singh entered into second development agreement the land to the co-accused Kashi Nath Jha fraudulently on 2017.
It is submitted by the learned Senior counsel on behalf of the petitioner that the facts as alleged, will not make out an offence under the Sections charged.

The development agreement was entered in the year 2008 but since for more than four years, no step was taken by the informant for development,
therefore, the petitioner was constrained to enter into development agreement with third party.
Petitioner had not entered into any development agreement with the informant, but had only witnessed the said agreement.

The matter is of civil nature and the informant has also filed Title Suit No.251 of 2020 for specific performance of agreement.
Learned A.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail.
It is submitted that in full knowledge of provision of agreement, the petitioner entered into second agreement with third party after receiving Rs.21,10,000/-.
Considering the submissions of learned counsel and the fact as discussed above, the bail application is allowed.

Accordingly, the petitioner named above shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Court below subject to the condition that one of the bailor(s) must be close relatives of the petitioner and that he shall not commit an offence, similar to the offence of which he is accused in the present case.
(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Sandeep/ Uploaded.
